title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit High
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the clutch pedal switch B circuit that is higher than it should be. The clutch pedal switch tells the computer when the clutch pedal is pressed, which matters for starting and cruise control.
symptoms: Engine may not crank with the clutch pressed
Cruise control may not work or may not cancel

causes.name: Open or broken wire in the clutch pedal switch circuit
Switch out of adjustment at the pedal
Wire shorted to another power circuit

checks: Check the connector for pushed-out or loose pins
Check the clutch pedal switch circuit for an open wire or a short to voltage
Test the clutch pedal switch against the factory specification
fix: Repair the open or shorted wire or bad connector; if the wiring is good, replace the clutch pedal switch.

title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the four-wheel-drive (4WD) switch, which tells the computers which four-wheel-drive mode has been selected.
symptoms: 4WD may not engage, or the 4WD light may flash
Wrong drive mode shown on the dash

causes.name: Broken or damaged wiring to the 4WD switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the 4WD switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the 4WD switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the 4WD switch.

title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The four-wheel-drive (4WD) switch is giving readings that don't match what the computer expects for the current conditions. The 4WD switch tells the computers which four-wheel-drive mode has been selected.
symptoms: 4WD may not engage, or the 4WD light may flash
Wrong drive mode shown on the dash

causes.name: Transfer case position sensor or shift motor problem
High resistance in the wiring or connector
Control module software needs an update

checks: Compare the 4WD switch reading with what it should be on a scan tool
Inspect the wiring and connector for corrosion or damage
fix: Correct any fluid or wiring problem first; if the readings are still wrong, replace the 4WD switch.

title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the four-wheel-drive (4WD) switch circuit that is lower than it should be. The 4WD switch tells the computers which four-wheel-drive mode has been selected.
symptoms: 4WD may not engage, or the 4WD light may flash
Wrong drive mode shown on the dash

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the 4WD switch circuit

checks: Inspect the 4WD switch wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the 4WD switch and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the 4WD switch.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
plain: The signal from the transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch G keeps dropping out or jumping around, which usually points to a loose connection or a damaged wire.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)
Problem may come and go, often over bumps

causes.name: Chafed wiring that opens or shorts as it moves

checks: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching live data
Look for rubbed-through wiring near brackets and moving parts
fix: Repair the loose connection or damaged wire; replace the pressure sensor/switch only if it fails testing.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The transmission computer is getting pressure readings from fluid pressure sensor/switch A that don't make sense for the gear and conditions. It often comes down to low or dirty fluid or a failing sensor.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Low, dirty or burnt transmission fluid
Blocked passage or sticking valve in the valve body

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition first
Compare the sensor reading with the gear selected on a scan tool
Inspect the sensor connector for fluid or corrosion
fix: Correct the fluid level and condition first; if the code returns, replace the pressure sensor/switch.
drive: Often drivable gently to a shop soon, sometimes with no symptoms. If shifting gets harsh, it stays in one gear or slips, keep trips short and avoid highways. Low fluid can cause this, so if you see a leak or a transmission warning, don't keep driving until it's checked.
test_first: Check fluid level first, then compare the pressure sensor reading to an actual line pressure gauge reading and inspect the wiring before replacing the sensor.

title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees a signal or voltage in the transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch A circuit that is lower than it should be. The pressure sensor/switch reports hydraulic pressure (or on some transmissions, the selected gear range) to the transmission computer.
symptoms: Transmission may stay in one gear (limp mode)

causes.name: Wire shorted to ground in the sensor circuit

checks: Inspect the pressure sensor/switch wiring for chafed spots touching metal
Check the circuit for a short to ground with a meter
Unplug the pressure sensor/switch and see whether the reading changes
fix: Fix any shorted or damaged wiring; if the wiring is good, replace the pressure sensor/switch.
drive: Use care. This can mean real low fluid pressure or just a sensor circuit fault. If shifting is normal, drive gently to a shop soon. If it slips, stays in one gear, or you see a leak or warning message, stop driving, because real low pressure can quickly damage the transmission.
test_first: Check fluid level, then verify actual line pressure with a gauge and test the sensor wiring for a short to ground before replacing the sensor.

title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
plain: The computer found an electrical problem in the circuit for the park/neutral position switch, which tells the engine computer when the transmission is in Park or Neutral.
symptoms: Engine may not crank, or may only crank in Neutral
Gear indicator or idle quality may be slightly off

causes.name: Switch or shift cable out of adjustment
Damaged wiring or connector at the switch
Blown fuse or missing power or ground

checks: Look over the wiring and connector at the park/neutral switch for damage, rubbing or corrosion
Check related fuses, power and ground with a meter
Test the park/neutral switch against the factory specification before replacing it
fix: Repair any wiring or connector fault found; if the circuit tests good, replace the park/neutral switch.
drive: Usually drivable, but the car may not start in Park, or might crank in gear. If the engine starts with the shifter in Drive or Reverse, don't drive it until it's fixed. Otherwise it's mostly an inconvenience; get it checked when you can and always set the parking brake.
test_first: Check the park/neutral switch reading on a scanner in each gear, its adjustment, the connector and the shift linkage before replacing the switch.
